title: Chapter 26. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — X: companions and followers
html:
Continuation and conclusion of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 26: GPT section 6.3 "Companions" (GPT1 pp. 451–489) — all eighteen padas signed Narahari (nos. 2, 4, 7, 8, 42–44, 49, 55, 58, 61, 62, 68, 69, 71, 72, 77, 83), and also one pada on the sannyasa found in the continuous check of signatures in sections 3.x, 4.x and 5.3–7 (GPT1 5.3, no. 7). The first padas of the section are about Gaura's companions (Gadadhara Pandita, Srivasa, Gadadhara Dasa, the circle of companions); then come padas about the followers of later generations: Shyamananda, the poet Jnanadasa, Srinivasa Acharya, Narottama, Ramachandra and Govinda Kaviraja and their disciples. Such padas are marked in the heading "late layer: on the followers": they are not Gaura-lila in the narrow sense but praises of the acharyas of the tradition through whom Gaura's mercy reached the following generations. The signatures of the section were checked throughout, in the OCR and on the scan; the 14th and 15th waves of the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR) and its conclusion, and the Gaura-charita-chintamani (GCC, kiranas 1 and 4), were read continuously at the relevant places. Not translated (outside the appendix): nos. 15, 41, 48, 54, 63, 82 — signed Ghanashyama; no. 13 — signed Papiya Shekhara (about Narahari Sarakara; the catalogue had counted it as Narahari's); no. 70 — signed Vallabha; no. 6 — no signature; the other padas of the section are by other poets. Pages 462–463 of GPT1 (no. 27, end, to no. 30) are missing from the scan: these padas were checked in GPT2 — signed Madho and Radhavallabha. The base text is GPT1 (by the scan), collated with GPT2, the BR (eds. 1912, 1960 and 2006) and the GCC (ed. 1947); the PK, KGC, PS, Gita-chandrodaya and Narottama-vilasa were checked. Pronouns referring to Gaura, Nityananda and Advaita are capitalized, those referring to the companions and followers are not. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced. At the end — a concluding note to the whole appendix.

1. Narahari — "dhanya dhanya bali mena…" (GPT1 pp. 452–453, section 6.3, no. 2)

The birth of Gadadhara Pandita: on the new-moon day of the month of Vaishakha, in the house of Madhava Mishra in Nadia, Gadadhara, Gauranga's beloved, was born; Madhava and Ratnavati are beside themselves with joy, the people of Nadia praise their fortune, the brahmanas' wives bless the infant, placing rice and durva grass on his head; the poet asks to sing Gadai's qualities birth after birth. Raga pahida. Attribution: not established — GPT only; plain Bengali tripadi; the GPT2 index does not assign it to Sarakara.1

ধন্য ধন্য বলি মেন, চারি যুগ মধ্যে হেন, কলির ভাগ্যে সীমা নাই ।
সুন্দর নদীয়া পুরে, মাধব মিশ্রের ঘরে, কি অদ্ভুত আনন্দ বাধাই ॥

dhanya dhanya bali mena, cāri yuga madhye hena, kalira bhāgye sīmā nāi |
sundara nadīyā pure, mādhaba miśrera ghare, ki adbhuta ānanda bādhāi ||

dhanya dhanya — glory, glory; bali — saying; mena (= yena) — as it were (here a particle; taken as "[all] say"); cāri yuga madhye — in the four yugas; hena — such; kalira bhāgye — to the fortune of Kali; sīmā nāi — there is no limit; sundara nadīyā pure — in the beautiful town of Nadia; mādhaba miśrera ghare — in the house of Madhava Mishra; ki adbhuta — what wondrous; ānanda bādhāi — rejoicing, festivity

1.1"Glory, glory!" all say: in all four yugas there was nothing like it — the fortune of Kali knows no limit: in beautiful Nadia, in the house of Madhava Mishra — what wondrous rejoicing!

বৈশাখের কুহু দিনে, জনমিলা শুভক্ষণে, গৌরাঙ্গের প্রিয় গদাধর ।
শ্রীমাধব রত্নাবতী, পুত্রমুখ দেখি অতি, উল্লাসে অধৈর্য্য নিরন্তর ॥

baiśākhera kuhu dine, janamilā śubhakṣaṇe, gaurāṅgera priya gadādhara |
śrīmādhaba ratnābatī, putramukha dekhi ati, ullāse adhairyya nirantara ||

baiśākhera kuhu dine — on the new-moon day of Vaishakha; janamilā — was born; śubhakṣaṇe — at an auspicious moment; gaurāṅgera priya — Gauranga's beloved; gadādhara — Gadadhara; śrī-mādhaba ratnābatī — Sri Madhava and Ratnavati; putramukha dekhi — seeing their son's face; ati ullāse — in great joy; adhairya nirantara — ceaselessly beside themselves

1.2On the new-moon day of Vaishakha, at an auspicious moment, Gadadhara, Gauranga's beloved, was born. Sri Madhava and Ratnavati, seeing their son's face, are beside themselves with joy.

কিবা গদাধরশোভা, সভার নয়নলোভা, যেন কত আনন্দের ধাম ।
ঝলমল করে বর্ণ, জিনিয়া সে শুদ্ধ স্বর্ণ, সর্ব্বাঙ্গ সুন্দর অনুপাম ॥

kibā gadādharaśobhā, sabhāra nayanalobhā, yena kata ānandera dhāma |
jhalamala kare barṇa, jiniyā se śuddha svarṇa, sarvvāṅga sundara anupāma ||

kibā — what; gadādhara-śobhā — Gadadhara's beauty; sabhāra nayana-lobhā — the delight of everyone's eyes; yena — as if; kata ānandera dhāma — the abode of every joy; jhalamala kare barṇa — his colour shines; jiniyā — surpassing; se śuddha svarṇa — pure gold; sarvāṅga sundara — his whole body beautiful; anupāma — incomparable

1.3What beauty Gadadhara has — a delight to the eyes of all, as if the abode of every joy! The colour of his skin shines, surpassing pure gold; his whole body is beautiful, incomparable.

যত নদীয়ার লোক, পাসরিয়া দুঃখ শোক, পরস্পর কহে কুতূহলে ।
মাধবের কিবা ভাগ্য, হৈল যেন রত্ন লভ্য, না জানি কতেক পুণ্যফলে ॥

yata nadīyāra loka, pāsariyā duḥkha śoka, paraspara kahe kutūhale |
mādhabera kibā bhāgya, haila yena ratna labhya, nā jāni kateka puṇyaphale ||

yata nadīyāra loka — all the people of Nadia; pāsariyā — forgetting; duḥkha śoka — grief and sorrow; paraspara kahe — say to one another; kutūhale — with delight; mādhabera kibā bhāgya — how fortunate Madhava is; haila yena ratna labhya — as if he gained a jewel; nā jāni — we do not know; kateka puṇya-phale — as the fruit of what merits

1.4All the people of Nadia, forgetting grief and sorrow, say to one another with delight: "How fortunate Madhava is — as if he had gained a jewel! We do not know for what merits!"

বিপ্রপত্নীগণ আসি, আনন্দ-সাগরে ভাসি, রত্নাবতী মায়ে প্রশংসিয়া ।
দেখিয়া সোণার সুতে, ধান দূর্ব্বা দিয়া মাথে, আশীর্ব্বাদ করে হর্ষ হৈয়া ॥

biprapatnīgaṇa āsi, ānanda-sāgare bhāsi, ratnābatī māye praśaṃsiyā |
dekhiyā soṇāra sute, dhāna dūrvvā diyā māthe, āśīrvvāda kare harṣa haiyā ||

bipra-patnī-gaṇa āsi — the brahmanas' wives, coming; ānanda-sāgare bhāsi — floating in an ocean of bliss; ratnābatī māye — mother Ratnavati; praśaṃsiyā — praising; dekhiyā soṇāra sute — seeing the golden son; dhāna dūrvā diyā māthe — placing rice and durva on his head; āśīrvāda kare — bless; harṣa haiyā — rejoicing

1.5The wives of the brahmanas come, floating in an ocean of bliss, praise mother Ratnavati, and, gazing on the golden son, place rice and durva grass on his head and joyfully bless him.

গদাধরপ্রভাবেতে, বিবিধ মঙ্গল যাতে, বন্দীগণ করে ধাওয়া ধাই ।
নরহরি কহে যেন, জনমে জনমে হেন, গদাইচাঁদের গুণ গাই ॥

gadādharaprabhābete, bibidha maṅgala yāte, bandīgaṇa kare dhāoyā dhāi |
narahari kahe yena, janame janame hena, gadāicām̐dera guṇa gāi ||

gadādhara-prabhābete — by Gadadhara's power; bibidha maṅgala — all kinds of auspicious [rites]; yāte — [take place]; bandī-gaṇa — the bards; kare dhāoyā dhāi — hasten one after another; narahari kahe — Narahari says; yena — may it be that; janame janame — birth after birth; hena — thus; gadāicām̐dera guṇa gāi — I sing the qualities of Gadaichand

1.6By Gadadhara's power all kinds of auspicious rites are performed; the bards hasten one after another [with praises]. Narahari says: "O that birth after birth I might sing Gadaichand's qualities just so!"2

the BR, GCC, Gita-chandrodaya, PK, KGC or PS. The reading in 1.1 "bali mena" (so in GPT1 and GPT2) is unclear; understood as "[all] say". C. Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (147–153) he is Sri Radha Herself, "the Lakshmi of Gaura's love". "The new moon of Vaishakha" (kuhu — the new moon) is the day of his appearance, as also in the Prema-vilasa (bilasa 22). The appearance of the Lord's eternal companion is not a birth under karma: he descends together with the Lord. Rice and durva grass on the head — a Bengali rite of blessing a newborn. Gadai, Gadaichand — affectionate names of Gadadhara.

2. Narahari — "gadādhara parama sughara rasadhāma…" (GPT1 p. 453, no. 4; GCC)

Gadadhara among the companions in the morning: his fair body captivates Kama; the smile of his lotus face is nectar; his speech eclipses the mantra that enchants the world; remembering his former pastimes he loses his composure; the poet smiles, seeing the hidden become manifest. Raga not specified ("yatharaga"). Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.3

গদাধর পরম সুঘর রসধাম ।
রুচির গৌর তনু তনুরুচি রুচিকর তছু নিরমঞ্ছন করু কত কাম ॥ ধ্রু ॥

gadādhara parama sughara rasadhāma |
rucira gaura tanu tanuruci rucikara tachu niramañchana karu kata kāma || dhru ||

gadādhara — Gadadhara; parama sughara — supreme elegance; rasa-dhāma — abode of rasa; rucira gaura tanu — the beautiful fair body; tanu-ruci rucikara — captivating in its lustre; tachu — his; niramañchana karu — offer themselves in expiation; kata kāma — how many Kamadevas

2.1Gadadhara is supreme elegance, an abode of rasa: to his beautiful fair body, captivating in its lustre, how many Kamadevas offer themselves in expiation!

ও মুখকমল কমলবনবিজিত সুচারু মকরন্দ সদৃশ মৃদুহাস ।
ঘন ঘন নয়ন-চষক ভরি ভরি পরি পীয়ত হিয় মধি অধিক উলাস ॥

o mukhakamala kamalabanabijita sucāru makaranda sadṛśa mṛduhāsa |
ghana ghana nayana-caṣaka bhari bhari pari pīyata hiya madhi adhika ulāsa ||

o mukha-kamala — that lotus face; kamalabana-bijita — that has conquered a forest of lotuses; sucāru makaranda sadṛśa — like lovely flower-nectar; mṛduhāsa — the gentle smile; ghana ghana — again and again; nayana-caṣaka — the cups of the eyes; bhari bhari pari — filling to the brim; pīyata — drinks; hiya madhi — in the heart; adhika ulāsa — great delight

2.2That lotus face, which has conquered a whole forest of lotuses; his gentle smile — like lovely flower-nectar; again and again, filling the cups of his eyes, he drinks — and in his heart there is great delight.

ও মৃদু মধুর বচন রচনা নব নিন্দিত জগবশীকরণ-সুমন্ত্র ।
শুনত লুব্ধ শ্রুতি শ্রুতিবাঞ্ছিত বহু বিসরিত বেদশ্রবণ শ্রুতিতন্ত্র ॥

o mṛdu madhura bacana racanā naba nindita jagabaśīkaraṇa-sumantra |
śunata lubdha śruti śrutibāñchita bahu bisarita bedaśrabaṇa śrutitantra ||

o mṛdu madhura bacana — that soft, sweet speech; racanā naba — ever new in its composition; nindita — eclipsing; jaga-baśīkaraṇa-sumantra — the excellent mantra that enchants the world; śunata — hearing; lubdha śruti — the greedy ears; śruti-bāñchita — coveted by the Vedas; bahu bisarita — utterly forget; beda-śrabaṇa — the hearing of the Vedas; śruti-tantra — the shrutis and tantras

2.3His soft, sweet speech, ever new, eclipses the mantra that enchants the world;
hearing it, greedy ears — coveted even by the Vedas — forget the hearing of Vedas and tantras.

পূরব চরিত চিত চিন্তি অথির ধৃতি গতি বিরহিত অতিশয় সুখে ভাসি ।
দূরে রহু হেম প্রেম নিরুপম বর নরহরি গুপত বেকত হেরি হাসি ॥

pūraba carita cita cinti athira dhṛti gati birahita atiśaya sukhe bhāsi |
dūre rahu hema prema nirupama bara narahari gupata bekata heri hāsi ||

pūraba carita — former pastimes; cita cinti — remembering in the heart; athira — unsteady; dhṛti gati birahita — bereft of composure and motion; atiśaya sukhe bhāsi — floating in boundless happiness; dūre rahu hema — away with gold; prema nirupama bara — peerless, excellent [is his] prema; narahari — Narahari; gupata bekata heri — seeing the hidden made manifest; hāsi — smiles

2.4Remembering in his heart his former pastimes, he loses steadiness, is bereft of motion and floats in boundless happiness. Away with gold! — so peerless is his prema; Narahari, seeing the hidden become manifest, smiles.4

in the morning the companions gather around Gaura, and the poet describes each of them), pada 17 ("yatharaga"; before it, pada 16 — also on Gadadhara, signed Narahari, not in the GPT; after it — Ghanashyama's pada on Narahari Sarakara = GPT no. 15). The variants are insignificant (in the OCR of the GCC the lines of 2.3 are distorted). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or Gita-chandrodaya. B. image of beauty before which the god of love fades. "Former pastimes" — the lila of Vraja: according to the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (147–153) Gadadhara Pandita is Sri Radha; in Gaura-lila he hides this bhava, but in ecstasy it shows through — this is "the hidden become manifest". "Away with gold" — neither the gold of his skin nor anything else compares with his prema. The subject in 2.2 (who "drinks") is not named: Gadadhara drinks Gaura's beauty with his eyes (so in the context of the GCC), or the onlookers drink the nectar of his smile.

3. Narahari — "ājuka sukha kachu baraṇe na jāta…" (GPT1 p. 454, no. 7; GCC)

Srivasa among the companions: seeing the Lord's play, he smiles softly; from love his body sways, his hairs stand on end as if he wore a jacket of kadamba flowers; he trembles like a creeper in the wind, repeats "Friend of the lowly!", sings, dances, weeps. Raga not specified ("yatharaga"). Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.5

আজুক সুখ কছু বরণে ন জাত ।
রসিক সুধীর সুঘর শ্রীবাস পহুঁ রঙ্গ হেরি মৃদু মৃদু মুসিকাত ॥ ধ্রু ॥

ājuka sukha kachu baraṇe na jāta |
rasika sudhīra sughara śrībāsa pahum̐ raṅga heri mṛdu mṛdu musikāta || dhru ||

ājuka sukha — today's happiness; kachu baraṇe na jāta — cannot at all be described; rasika — knower of rasa; sudhīra — wise; sughara — elegant; śrībāsa — Srivasa; pahum̐ raṅga heri — seeing the Lord's play; mṛdu mṛdu musikāta — smiles very softly

3.1Today's happiness cannot be described in words:
Srivasa — knower of rasa, wise and elegant — seeing the Lord's play, smiles very softly.

সুবলিত দেহ নেহভরে টলমল ললিত ভঙ্গী নিরুপম ছবি ভারী ।
অবিরল পুলক কদম্ব লসত জনু পহিরল কঞ্চু পরম রুচিকারী ॥

subalita deha nehabhare ṭalamala lalita bhaṅgī nirupama chabi bhārī |
abirala pulaka kadamba lasata janu pahirala kañcu parama rucikārī ||

subalita deha — the stately body; nehabhare ṭalamala — sways with love; lalita bhaṅgī — graceful bearing; nirupama chabi bhārī — incomparable great beauty; abirala pulaka — the dense thrill of hairs; kadamba lasata — shines [like] kadamba; janu — as if; pahirala kañcu — he had put on a jacket; parama rucikārī — most beautiful

3.2His stately body sways with love; graceful is his bearing, incomparable his wondrous beauty; his thickly risen hairs shine as if he had put on a most beautiful jacket of kadamba flowers.

বাতাতুর লতিকা সম কম্প ন শকত সম্ভারি বিবশ রসপূর ।
দীনবন্ধু কত বদত নিরন্তর অন্তর তরল রহল ধৃতি দূর ॥

bātātura latikā sama kampa na śakata sambhāri bibaśa rasapūra |
dīnabandhu kata badata nirantara antara tarala rahala dhṛti dūra ||

bātātura latikā sama — like a creeper tormented by the wind; kampa — he trembles; na śakata sambhāri — cannot master [himself]; bibaśa rasa-pūra — helpless in the flood of rasa; dīnabandhu — "Friend of the lowly"; kata badata nirantara — repeats ceaselessly; antara tarala — his heart melts; rahala dhṛti dūra — steadiness has gone far away

3.3He trembles like a creeper in the wind and cannot master himself, helpless in the flood of rasa; ceaselessly he repeats: "Friend of the lowly!" — his heart melts, and steadiness has left him.

সুন্দর গুণগণ গাওত লঘু লঘু নাচত নয়নে বহত জলধার ।
নরহরি ভণ অনুভব ন হোত হিয় উপজত কত কত ভাব বিকার ॥

sundara guṇagaṇa gāota laghu laghu nācata nayane bahata jaladhāra |
narahari bhaṇa anubhaba na hota hiya upajata kata kata bhāba bikāra ||

sundara guṇagaṇa gāota — he sings the beautiful qualities; laghu laghu nācata — lightly dances; nayane bahata jaladhāra — streams of tears flow from his eyes; narahari bhaṇa — says Narahari; anubhaba na hota — one cannot fathom; hiya upajata — arise in the heart; kata kata bhāba-bikāra — how many stirrings of bhava

3.4He sings the beautiful qualities [of the Lord], lightly dances, streams of tears flow from his eyes. Narahari says: one cannot fathom how many stirrings of bhava arise in his heart.6

pada 19 ("yatharaga"). Variants: 3.3 "dīnabandhu" by the GCC and the GPT1 scan (GPT1 OCR — "bīṇa bandhu"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS or Gita-chandrodaya. B. "A jacket of kadamba flowers" — the thrill of the hairs (pulaka), like the knobbly kadamba flower. "Friend of the lowly" (dīnabandhu) — an address to the Lord.

4. Narahari — "sundara sughara gadādhara dāsa…" (GPT1 p. 454, no. 8; GCC)

Gadadhara Dasa beside Gaura — like a moon beside the moon; his tender body eclipses the champaka flower; his eyes are languid; former bhavas arise ceaselessly in his heart, and however much he hides them, he cannot. Raga not specified ("yatharaga"). Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.7

সুন্দর সুঘর গদাধর দাস ।
গুণমণি গৌরসমীপ বিলসত জনু চন্দ নিকট হি চন্দ পরকাশ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

sundara sughara gadādhara dāsa |
guṇamaṇi gaurasamīpa bilasata janu canda nikaṭa hi canda parakāśa || dhru ||

sundara sughara — beautiful, elegant; gadādhara dāsa — Gadadhara Dasa; guṇamaṇi gaura-samīpa — beside Gaura, the jewel of qualities; bilasata — shines; janu — as if; canda nikaṭa hi — beside the moon; canda parakāśa — a moon had risen

4.1Beautiful, elegant is Gadadhara Dasa:
beside Gaura, the jewel of qualities, he shines as if beside the moon another moon had risen.

মৃদুতর দেহ নেহময় মধুরিম মাধুরী করু চম্পক-মদ-খীন ।
ধৃতিভর-ভঞ্জনকারী ভঙ্গী ভুব রঞ্জন কঞ্জ-চরণ গতিহীন ॥

mṛdutara deha nehamaya madhurima mādhurī karu campaka-mada-khīna |
dhṛtibhara-bhañjanakārī bhaṅgī bhuba rañjana kañja-caraṇa gatihīna ||

caitanyera priya yata — all who are dear to Chaitanya; kare sneha abirata — love [him] ceaselessly; kahite ki jāni guṇagaṇa — how can I tell his virtues; alapa bayasa haite — from his early years; bidyāya nipuṇa — skilled in learning; cite cinte sadā — always meditated in his heart; caitanya-caraṇa — on Chaitanya's feet

10.2All who are dear to Chaitanya love him ceaselessly — how can I tell his virtues?
Skilled in learning from his early years, he always meditated on Chaitanya's feet.

একদিন রাত্রিশেষে, শ্রীচৈতন্য স্নেহাবেশে, নিতাইচাঁদেরে সঙ্গে লৈয়া ।
শ্রীনিবাস পাশে আসি, স্বপ্নচ্ছলে হাসি হাসি, কহে শ্রীনিবাস মুখ চাঞা ॥

ekadina rātriśeṣe, śrīcaitanya snehābeśe, nitāicām̐dere saṅge laiyā |
śrīnibāsa pāśe āsi, svapnacchale hāsi hāsi, kahe śrīnibāsa mukha cāñā ||

ekadina rātriśeṣe — one day at the end of the night; śrī-caitanya snehābeśe — Sri Chaitanya, full of love; nitāicām̐dere saṅge laiyā — taking Nitaichand with Him; śrīnibāsa pāśe āsi — coming to Srinivasa; svapnacchale — in a dream; hāsi hāsi — smiling; kahe — says; śrīnibāsa mukha cāñā — looking into Srinivasa's face

10.3One day, at the end of the night, Sri Chaitanya, full of love, taking Nitaichand with Him, came to Srinivasa and in a dream, smiling, spoke, looking into his face:

যাবে শীঘ্র বৃন্দাবন, তথা রূপ সনাতন, রচিল বিচিত্র গ্রন্থগণ ।
বিতরিব তোমা দ্বারে, এত কহি বারে বারে, নিত্যানন্দে কৈল সমর্পণ ॥

yābe śīghra bṛndābana, tathā rūpa sanātana, racila bicitra granthagaṇa |
bitariba tomā dvāre, eta kahi bāre bāre, nityānande kaila samarpaṇa ||

yābe śīghra bṛndābana — go quickly to Vrindavana; tathā rūpa sanātana — there Rupa and Sanatana; racila bicitra granthagaṇa — have written wonderful books; bitariba tomā dvāre — I shall distribute through you; eta kahi bāre bāre — saying this again and again; nityānande kaila samarpaṇa — He entrusted [him] to Nityananda

10.4"Go quickly to Vrindavana: there Rupa and Sanatana have written wonderful books — through you I shall distribute them." Saying this, again and again He entrusted him to Nityananda.

হেন কালে স্বপ্নভঙ্গ, ধরিতে নারয় অঙ্গ, শ্রীনিবাস ব্যাকুল হইলা ।
নীলাচল গৌড়দেশে, ভ্রমিয়া সে প্রেমাবেশে, বৃন্দাবন গমন করিলা ॥

hena kāle svapnabhaṅga, dharite nāraya aṅga, śrīnibāsa byākula hailā |
nīlācala gauṛadeśe, bhramiyā se premābeśe, bṛndābana gamana karilā ||

hena kāle — then; svapna-bhaṅga — the dream broke; dharite nāraya aṅga — could not contain himself; śrīnibāsa byākula hailā — Srinivasa was filled with longing; nīlācala gauṛadeśe — through Nilachala and Gauda; bhramiyā — wandering; se premābeśe — in the ecstasy of love; bṛndābana gamana karilā — set out for Vrindavana

10.5Then the dream broke — Srinivasa could not contain himself and was filled with longing; having wandered in the ecstasy of love through Nilachala and Gauda, he set out for Vrindavana.

কত অভিলাষ মনে, উলাসে অলপদিনে, মথুরানগরে প্রবেশিল ।
শ্রীরূপ শ্রীসনাতন, এ দুঁহার অদর্শন, শুনি তথা মূর্চ্ছিত হইল ॥

kata abhilāṣa mane, ulāse alapadine, mathurānagare prabeśila |
śrīrūpa śrīsanātana, e dum̐hāra adarśana, śuni tathā mūrcchita haila ||

kata abhilāṣa mane — with great hopes in his heart; ulāse — rejoicing; alapa dine — in a few days; mathurā-nagare prabeśila — reached the city of Mathura; śrī-rūpa śrī-sanātana — Sri Rupa and Sri Sanatana; e dum̐hāra adarśana — the disappearance of these two; śuni tathā — hearing there; mūrcchita haila — fainted

10.6With great hopes, rejoicing, in a few days he reached the city of Mathura;
there, hearing of the disappearance of Sri Rupa and Sri Sanatana, he fainted.

কাঁদয়ে চেতন পাঞা, কহে ভূমে লোটাইয়া, হাহা প্রভু রূপ সনাতন ।
কি লাগি বঞ্চিত কৈলা, না বুঝি এসব খেলা, কি লাগিয়া রাখিলা জীবন ॥

kām̐daye cetana pāñā, kahe bhūme loṭāiyā, hāhā prabhu rūpa sanātana |
ki lāgi bañcita kailā, nā bujhi esaba khelā, ki lāgiyā rākhilā jībana ||

kām̐daye cetana pāñā — coming to, he weeps; kahe bhūme loṭāiyā — says, rolling on the ground; hāhā prabhu rūpa sanātana — alas, my masters Rupa and Sanatana; ki lāgi bañcita kailā — why did you deprive [me]; nā bujhi e saba khelā — I do not understand this play; ki lāgiyā rākhilā jībana — why did you keep me alive

10.7Coming to, he weeps and, rolling on the ground, says: "Alas, alas, my masters Rupa and Sanatana! Why have you deprived me? I do not understand this play! Why have you kept me alive?"

ঐছে খেদযুক্ত মন, জানি রূপ সনাতন, স্বপ্নচ্ছলে আসি প্রেমাবেশে ।
শ্রীনিবাস কোলে লৈয়া, নেত্রবারি নিবারিয়া, কহে অতি সুমধুর ভাষে ॥

aiche khedayukta mana, jāni rūpa sanātana, svapnacchale āsi premābeśe |
śrīnibāsa kole laiyā, netrabāri nibāriyā, kahe ati sumadhura bhāṣe ||

aiche kheda-yukta mana — such a grief-stricken mind; jāni — knowing; rūpa sanātana — Rupa and Sanatana; svapnacchale āsi — coming in a dream; premābeśe — in the ecstasy of love; śrīnibāsa kole laiyā — taking Srinivasa on their laps; netrabāri nibāriyā — wiping his tears; kahe ati sumadhura bhāṣe — say in the sweetest words

10.8Knowing his grief-stricken mind, Rupa and Sanatana in the ecstasy of love came to him in a dream, took Srinivasa on their laps, wiped away his tears and said in the sweetest words:

শীঘ্র গিয়া বৃন্দাবন, কর আত্মসমর্পণ, শ্রীগোপাল ভট্টের চরণে ।
না ভাবিবে কোন দুখ, পাইবে পরম সুখ, ঐছে দেখা দিব দুই জনে ॥

śīghra giyā bṛndābana, kara ātmasamarpaṇa, śrīgopāla bhaṭṭera caraṇe |
nā bhābibe kona dukha, pāibe parama sukha, aiche dekhā diba dui jane ||

śīghra giyā bṛndābana — going quickly to Vrindavana; kara ātmasamarpaṇa — surrender yourself; śrī-gopāla bhaṭṭera caraṇe — at the feet of Sri Gopala Bhatta; nā bhābibe kona dukha — do not think of any sorrow; pāibe parama sukha — you will attain the highest happiness; aiche dekhā diba dui jane — thus we two will appear

10.9"Go quickly to Vrindavana and surrender at the feet of Sri Gopala Bhatta; do not think of any sorrow — you will attain the highest happiness; thus we two will appear to you."

এত কহি অদর্শন, হৈল রূপ সনাতন, শ্রীনিবাস প্রভাতে উঠিয়া ।
প্রবেশয়ে বৃন্দাবনে, প্রেমধারা দুনয়নে, বৃন্দাবনশোভা নিরখিয়া ॥

eta kahi adarśana, haila rūpa sanātana, śrīnibāsa prabhāte uṭhiyā |
prabeśaye bṛndābane, premadhārā dunayane, bṛndābanaśobhā nirakhiyā ||

eta kahi — saying this; adarśana haila — vanished; rūpa sanātana — Rupa and Sanatana; śrīnibāsa prabhāte uṭhiyā — Srinivasa, rising at dawn; prabeśaye bṛndābane — enters Vrindavana; premadhārā dunayane — streams of prema from both eyes; bṛndābana-śobhā nirakhiyā — gazing at the beauty of Vrindavana

10.10Saying this, Rupa and Sanatana vanished; Srinivasa, rising at dawn,
entered Vrindavana — streams of prema from both eyes — gazing at the beauty of Vrindavana.

শ্রীজীব শ্রীশ্রীনিবাসে, পাইয়া আনন্দাবেশে, গোস্বামিগণেরে মিলাইল ।
শ্রীরূপের স্বপ্নাদেশে, অতি স্নেহে শ্রীনিবাসে, শ্রীগোপালভট্ট শিষ্য কৈল ॥

śrījība śrīśrīnibāse, pāiyā ānandābeśe, gosvāmigaṇere milāila |
śrīrūpera svapnādeśe, ati snehe śrīnibāse, śrīgopālabhaṭṭa śiṣya kaila ||

śrī-jība — Sri Jiva; śrī-śrīnibāse pāiyā — having found Sri Srinivasa; ānandābeśe — in bliss; gosvāmigaṇere milāila — introduced [him] to the Gosvamis; śrī-rūpera svapnādeśe — by Sri Rupa's command in a dream; ati snehe — with great love; śrīnibāse — Srinivasa; śrī-gopāla-bhaṭṭa śiṣya kaila — Sri Gopala Bhatta made his disciple

10.11Sri Jiva, having found Sri Srinivasa, in bliss introduced him to the Gosvamis; by Sri Rupa's command in a dream, Sri Gopala Bhatta with great love made Srinivasa his disciple.

শ্রীজীব গোস্বামীর যত, স্নেহ কে কহিবে কত, করাইলা শাস্ত্রে বিচক্ষণ ।
শ্রীবাস আনন্দ মনে, প্রিয় নরোত্তম সনে, কিছু দিনে হইলা মিলন ॥

śrījība gosvāmīra yata, sneha ke kahibe kata, karāilā śāstre bicakṣaṇa |
śrībāsa ānanda mane, priya narottama sane, kichu dine hailā milana ||

śrī-jība gosvāmīra yata sneha — how much Sri Jiva Gosvami loved; ke kahibe kata — who can tell; karāilā śāstre bicakṣaṇa — made [him] learned in the shastras; śrībāsa — Srinivasa (shortened); ānanda mane — joyful at heart; priya narottama sane — with dear Narottama; kichu dine hailā milana — after some days met

10.12Who can tell how much Sri Jiva Gosvami loved him! He made him learned in the shastras; and Srinivasa, joyful at heart, after some days met dear Narottama.

নরোত্তমে লৈয়া সঙ্গে, ব্রজে ভ্রমিলেন রঙ্গে, গোবিন্দের আজ্ঞামালা পাঞা ।
গোস্বামীর গ্রন্থগণ, করিলেন বিতরণ, শ্রীগৌড়মণ্ডলে স্থির হৈয়া ॥

narottame laiyā saṅge, braje bhramilena raṅge, gobindera ājñāmālā pāñā |
gosvāmīra granthagaṇa, karilena bitaraṇa, śrīgauṛamaṇḍale sthira haiyā ||

narottame laiyā saṅge — taking Narottama with him; braje bhramilena raṅge — joyfully went round Vraja; gobindera ājñāmālā pāñā — receiving Govinda's garland of command; gosvāmīra granthagaṇa — the Gosvamis' books; karilena bitaraṇa — distributed; śrī-gauṛa-maṇḍale sthira haiyā — settling in Sri Gauda-mandala

10.13Taking Narottama with him, he joyfully went round Vraja and, receiving Govinda's garland of command, distributed the Gosvamis' books, settling in Sri Gauda-mandala.

গৌর প্রেমসুধাপানে, সদা মত্ত সংকীর্ত্তনে, জগতে ঘোষয়ে যশ যার ।
কহে নরহরি দীনে, উদ্ধারে আপন গুণে, এমন দয়াল নাহি আর ॥

gaura premasudhāpāne, sadā matta saṃkīrttane, jagate ghoṣaye yaśa yāra |
kahe narahari dīne, uddhāre āpana guṇe, emana dayāla nāhi āra ||

gaura prema-sudhā-pāne — drinking the nectar of Gaura's prema; sadā matta saṅkīrtane — ever intoxicated with sankirtana; jagate ghoṣaye yaśa yāra — whose fame resounds in the world; kahe narahari dīne — says lowly Narahari; uddhāre āpana guṇe — he saves by his own goodness; emana dayāla nāhi āra — there is no other so merciful

10.14Drinking the nectar of Gaura's prema, ever intoxicated with sankirtana, he is famed in the world. Lowly Narahari says: "He saves [the fallen] by his own goodness — there is no one so merciful."20

(ed. 1912, pp. ≈1048–1049; ed. 1960, 14.195–208, "the song of the life of Sri Srinivasa Acharya — in song, kamoda"): after the festival at Boraquli, Srinivasa with his disciples at Yajigrama spends his days in discussing the shastras and in sankirtana; "who does not sing of the Acharya's life?" (14.194), then this pada and Govindadasa's pada (GPT no. 57). Variants: 10.4 in the OCR of BR-1960 the stanza is longer ("parama karuṇābān", "śrīnibāse kole laiyā" — probably an OCR fault: these words come from 10.1 and 10.8); 10.12 BR "śrībāsa ānandamane … kichu dine haila milana"; the rest orthographic. Not in the GCC, PK, KGC, PS or Gita-chandrodaya. B. Sanatana in a dream — vilasa 6): the dream in which Mahaprabhu entrusts Srinivasa to Nityananda and sends him to Vrindavana; the news of Rupa's and Sanatana's passing in Mathura; their appearance in a dream; initiation from Gopala Bhatta; study under Jiva; the meeting with Narottama; the garland from the Deity Govinda as the command to take the books to Gauda. "Srinivasa" in 10.12 is called "śrībāsa" — a shortening of the name for the metre (not Srivasa Pandita). A dream in which the Lord and His associates appear is not a play of imagination but their mercy (svapna-darshana).

11. Narahari — "jaya jaya śrīnarottama parama udāra…" (GPT1 p. 476, no. 61; BR)

Late layer: on the followers. The form of Narottama: he delights the world, shines like a golden lotus, as if ceaselessly pouring nectar; his body thrills, a smile is on his face, his eyes are full of compassion, his speech enchants; tilaka, tulasi-mala, blue garments; his cool, tender feet shine in the poet's heart. Raga belabali. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (14th wave, Budhari).21

জয় জয় শ্রীনরোত্তম পরম উদার ।
জগজনরঞ্জন কনক কঞ্জরুচি জনু মকরন্দ বরিখে অনিবার ॥ ধ্রু ॥

jaya jaya śrīnarottama parama udāra |
jagajanarañjana kanaka kañjaruci janu makaranda barikhe anibāra || dhru ||

jaya jaya — glory, glory; śrī-narottama — to Sri Narottama; parama udāra — boundlessly generous; jaga-jana-rañjana — delighting the people of the world; kanaka-kañja-ruci — shining like a golden lotus; janu — as if; makaranda barikhe anibāra — ceaselessly pouring nectar

11.1Glory, glory to Sri Narottama, boundlessly generous! He delights the people of the world, shines like a golden lotus — as if ceaselessly pouring nectar.

ঝলমল বিপুল পুলক কুল মণ্ডিত নিরুপম বদনে নিরত মৃদু হাস ।
টলমল নয়ন করুণ রসরঞ্জিত হরই শ্রবণ মন বচন বিলাস ॥

jhalamala bipula pulaka kula maṇḍita nirupama badane nirata mṛdu hāsa |
ṭalamala nayana karuṇa rasarañjita harai śrabaṇa mana bacana bilāsa ||

jhalamala — gleaming; bipula pulaka-kula maṇḍita — adorned with an abundant thrill of hairs; nirupama badane — on the peerless face; nirata mṛdu hāsa — an unfailing gentle smile; ṭalamala nayana — quivering eyes; karuṇa-rasa-rañjita — tinged with the rasa of compassion; haraī śrabaṇa mana — steals ear and mind; bacana-bilāsa — the play of speech

11.2An abundant thrill of the hairs gleams, on his peerless face — an unfailing gentle smile; his eyes quiver, tinged with the rasa of compassion; the play of his speech steals ear and mind.

নিরুপম তিলক ললাট মধুরতর তুলসী মাল কুলকণ্ঠ উজোর ।
সুবলনি বাহু ললিত কর পল্লব পরিসর উর উপমা নহ থোর ॥

nirupama tilaka lalāṭa madhuratara tulasī māla kulakaṇṭha ujora |
subalani bāhu lalita kara pallaba parisara ura upamā naha thora ||

nirupama tilaka — peerless tilaka; lalāṭa madhuratara — most charming brow; tulasī māla kula — necklaces of tulasi; kaṇṭha ujora — the neck shines; subalani bāhu — beautifully formed arms; lalita kara pallava — tender hand-shoots; parisara ura — broad chest; upamā naha thora — no comparison for it

11.3A peerless tilaka on a most charming brow, his neck shines with a necklace of tulasi; his arms are beautifully formed, his hands tender shoots, his broad chest — there is no comparison for it.

কটিতট ক্ষীণ নীল নব অম্বর পীন প্রবর উরু গঢ়ল সুঠার ।
কোমল চরণ যুগল অতি শীতল বিলসত নরহরি হৃদয় মাঝার ॥

kaṭitaṭa kṣīṇa nīla naba ambara pīna prabara uru gaṛhala suṭhāra |
komala caraṇa yugala ati śītala bilasata narahari hṛdaya mājhāra ||

kaṭitaṭa kṣīṇa — slender waist; nīla naba ambara — new blue garments; pīna prabara uru — full strong thighs; gaṛhala suṭhāra — beautifully sculpted; komala caraṇa yugala — both tender feet; ati śītala — most cool; bilasata — shine; narahari hṛdaya mājhāra — in Narahari's heart

11.4A slender waist, new blue garments, full strong thighs as if sculpted;
his tender feet, both most cool, shine in Narahari's heart.22

p. ≈1038; ed. 1960, 14.83–86, "in song, belabali"): at Budhari "the beauty of Sri Narottama intoxicates all; who does not sing of his form and virtues?" (14.82), then this pada; after it — "the circle of Vaishnavas is beautiful, the radiance of all is like the sun" and the departure for Boraquli (14.87–89). Variants: 11.4 BR "pīna prabara uru gaṛhala sāra" (GPT "suṭhāra"); the rest orthographic. Not in the GCC, PK, KGC, PS or Gita-chandrodaya. B. Prema-bhakti-candrika and the Prarthana, a great kirtaniya. The description of the form "from head to foot" (nakha-shikha) is a usual genre of songs about saints; here it is contemplation of a Vaishnava's form, not worldly admiration. "Shine in the heart" — the poet meditates on Narottama's feet as his refuge.

12. Narahari — "o mora karuṇāmaya, śrīṭhākura mahāśaya…" (GPT1 pp. 476–477, no. 62; BR)

Late layer: on the followers. The life of Narottama: young, he left royal pleasures and went to Vraja, received initiation from Lokanatha, became friends with Srinivasa — "one life in two bodies"; returning to Gauda, he visited Navadvipa and Nilachala; at Kheturi he serves six Deities; in his sankirtana the fortunate saw Gaurachandra dancing with Advaita, Nityananda and the companions; the poet longs to roll in the dust in tears with Narottama's name. Concluding note to the appendix

The appendix "Padas signed 'Narahari' from the Gaura-pada-tarangini" (chapters 17–26) is complete: 241 padas have been translated — all the padas signed Narahari known only from the GPT (with their witnesses — the Bhakti-ratnakara, the Gaura-charita-chintamani, the Gita-chandrodaya), except the padas in nagari-bhava (they will form a separate section with an introductory note). Attribution as marked in the headings: "probably Sarakara" — 4 (mangalacharana and Gaura's form: plain Bengali, not in the BR, assigned to Sarakara by the GPT2 index; authority C); "probably Chakravarti" — 221 (almost all found in the Bhakti-ratnakara or in the Gaura-charita-chintamani of Narahari Chakravarti, and one stands in the author's conclusion of the BR; authority B); "not established" — 16 (GPT only; among them several late padas, written apparently after both Naraharis; authority C); no pada of the appendix has authority D (doubtful authenticity). The result of the continuous check: the great majority of the "Narahari" padas known only from the GPT belong to Narahari Chakravarti (Ghanashyama Dasa), an 18th-century author who wove his songs into his accounts of the holy places and of the Lord's associates; the legacy of Narahari Sarakara, Mahaprabhu's companion, is above all the padas preserved in the Padakalpataru (the main part, chapters 1–6). Left outside the appendix: the padas in nagari-bhava (a separate section), the padas signed Ghanashyama, prayers to the guru and praises of poets without Gaura-lila, padas in which Narahari is only mentioned while the signature is another's, and one pada on Advaita known only from the BR (12th wave, vv. 3755–3760).
